original_title: Research on the water-sensitivity characteristics and consolidation mechanism of biopolymer-modified dispersive soils
title: Guar gum and xanthan gum keep dispersive soil from washing away
blurb: Dispersive soil erodes easily and is prone to piping and gully formation, a real headache for infrastructure in arid regions. They dose it with guar gum and xanthan gum and run permeability, disintegration, XRD, FTIR, and SEM to work out how the biopolymers change the soil's dispersion behavior and consolidation. Standard biopolymer-stabilization playbook, but the mechanistic characterization here goes deeper than most.

original_title: Bayesian optimization maps product yield and selectivity Pareto front solutions in biocatalytic PET degradation
title: Bayesian optimization finds the sweet spot for enzymatically recycling PET
blurb: Enzymes can break PET down to BHET for closed-loop resynthesis, but push too hard and you get MHET, terephthalic acid, and ethylene glycol instead of the monomer you actually want. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization maps the Pareto front between yield and selectivity, so instead of guessing at conditions you get the actual trade-off curve to pick from.

original_title: Compact red-shifted near-infrared fluorescent proteins enable deep-tissue SWIR imaging with in vivo optical clearing.
title: Near-infrared fluorescent proteins pushed further into the SWIR window
blurb: Three new monomeric NIR fluorescent proteins, miRFP729nano, 732nano and 735nano, engineered from a cyanobacteriochrome GAF domain, compact at 19.1 kDa and binding biliverdin, with emission maxima out to 735 nm. Their off-peak tail past 1000 nm runs several-fold brighter than the previous SWIR workhorse miRFP718nano, and miRFP732nano already doubles as a fusion tag. Small gain in brightness, but that's exactly what deep-tissue SWIR imaging lives on.

title: Cationic hydrogels from plant oil, built to carry proteins

original_title: Regiodivergent oxyfuctionalization of tricyclic “new-to-nature” terpenoids using structurally divergent unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs)
title: Screening 17 peroxygenases to functionalize terpenoids that don't exist in nature
blurb: Unspecific peroxygenases are good at regioselective C-H oxidation, but nobody had thrown them at bulky, non-natural terpene skeletons before. They screen 17 structurally distinct UPOs against tricyclic terpenoids made via BcBOT2 cyclization of non-natural farnesyl diphosphate analogs, and get regiodivergent outcomes on the same scaffold depending on which enzyme runs it. Basically assembling a toolkit for late-stage oxidation of molecules chemistry hasn't seen before.

original_title: Highly stable quasi-solid-state initially anode-free lithium metal batteries enabled by dynamic integrated interface engineering
title: An Ag additive that keeps anode-free lithium batteries from dying young
blurb: Anode-free lithium metal batteries promise more energy density with less manufacturing hassle, but poor reversibility of lithium plating and stripping usually kills them fast. The fix is an electrolyte additive built around Ag+ paired with Lewis-acid-generating anions, which triggers in-situ polymerization at the electrode-electrolyte interface and yields a quasi-solid-state cell that stays stable. A silver salt doing interface engineering is a neat trick, if it holds up outside the lab.
